The match began with intense争夺 in the opening 20 minutes. After a "cooling break", both sides received a yellow card each — England's midfielder Elliot Anderson and Argentina's centre-back Lisandro Martínez. Before half-time, the home fans cheered almost every whistle while booing the visitors' fouls.

The two teams went into the break level, and after switching ends the second half got underway. In the 55th minute, England's Anthony Gordon latched onto a pass and fired home to break the deadlock, putting England 1-0 ahead. The England fans in the stadium immediately erupted in wild celebration.

Trailing Argentina quickly launched a counter-attack, creating three crosses from the right within ten minutes, but all were blocked, drawing sighs from many Argentina supporters. In the 85th minute, Enzo Fernández met a cross from Messi to head home the equaliser, making it 1-1. Argentina's fans immediately started drumming in celebration, with whistles ringing around the stadium.

In stoppage time in the 92nd minute, Messi set up Lautaro Martínez to seal the victory, helping Argentina reach another final where they will face Spain for the World Cup crown. Argentina's fans once again went into raptures; even after the referee blew the final whistle, supporters continued to embrace in celebration, with some holding up cardboard cutouts of Messi.

Argentina fan Ho has supported Messi since he rose to prominence at Barcelona, and today turned out wearing the Argentina "two-star" number 10 jersey. He pointed out that this World Cup is Messi's farewell tournament and the team must work hard to defend their title. He believes that amid the controversy surrounding Messi and the team at this tournament, rather than arguing with fans over every decision, supporters should cherish the final chapter of Messi serving the national team. He joked that being young and strong, staying up late is no problem at all — but he…

England fans have been singing "Football's coming home!" throughout the tournament, yet once again failed to bring football home. Deaken, who is studying in the UK and returned to Hong Kong for the summer holidays, draped himself in the England flag today and cheered loudly with friends amid the intense action. He said it was his first time watching football in a mall to soak up the atmosphere, and felt that although fans from both sides were fully invested, they respected each other and there were no heated clashes.

When your supported team loses, disappointment is inevitable. Deaken, who shares a name with England midfielder Declan Rice, felt England put in a fairly respectable performance. Having been through two World Cups, he put it bluntly: "We've waited 60 years — what's another four years, it's no big deal!"

Argentina will face Spain on the 20th, bidding to defend their title; the third-place play-off on the 19th pits England against France.
